revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Bridge Engineering
revealWordProblem.text: The Golden Gate Bridge's two main cables are each about 7,650 feet long. A supply company sells cable-protection wrap in spools measured in yards. How many yards of protective wrap does one full cable need? Show your work using a conversion factor.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: 1 yard = 3 feet, so converting feet to the larger unit (yards) means dividing by the conversion factor: 7,650 ÷ 3 = 2,550 yards. One cable needs 2,550 yards of protective wrap.

conceptIntro.heading: The Big Ideas — Lessons 3.4–3.10
conceptIntro.intro: Here is the one thing to remember from each lesson, plus a quick guided example. If one of these feels shaky, that lesson is right above this one in the menu — you can open it any time.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: 3.4: The points from equal ratios form a straight line that passes through the origin (0, 0). • 3.5: Compare ratios fairly by making one part equal or by finding the unit rate. • 3.6: Find the scale factor, then multiply both parts; cross-multiply to check a proportion. • 3.7: Find the unit rate by dividing, then multiply it to find the amount you need. • 3.8: Divide the price by the number of items to get the cost per unit. The lower cost per unit is the better buy. • 3.9: Multiply or divide both numbers by the same amount to make an equivalent ratio. • 3.10: Multiply when changing to a smaller unit, and divide when changing to a bigger unit.

Lesson 3.10 — Convert Measurement Units: Multiply when changing to a smaller unit, and divide when changing to a bigger unit.

optional.stem: (Lesson 3.4) Recipe: 1 cup berries to 2 scoops yogurt. With cups on x and scoops on y, which pair shows 3 cups?
optional.explanation: Cups (x) come first, scoops (y) second. 3 cups need 3 × 2 = 6 scoops, so the point is (3, 6).
choiceFeedback: You doubled it, but check if that's the right scale factor.
Re-check how many times you need to multiply or scale.
This pairs 3 cups with 3 scoops, which would be 1 scoop per cup. Reread the recipe to see how many scoops a single cup needs.
optional.stemEs: Receta: 1 taza de bayas por 2 cucharadas de yogur. Con las tazas en x y las cucharadas en y, ¿cuál par muestra 3 tazas?
optional.explanationEs: Las tazas (x) van primero y las cucharadas (y) segundo. 3 tazas necesitan 3 × 2 = 6 cucharadas, así que el punto es (3, 6).
hints: On this graph the x-coordinate always stands for cups and the y-coordinate always stands for scoops.
Work out the scoops that go with 3 cups first, then write the pair with cups in front.
The recipe uses 2 scoops for every 1 cup, so 3 cups means 3 groups of 2 scoops. Find that total and put it second in the pair.
hintsEs: En esta gráfica, la coordenada x siempre representa las tazas y la coordenada y siempre representa las cucharadas.
Calcula primero las cucharadas que corresponden a 3 tazas y luego escribe el par con las tazas al frente.
La receta usa 2 cucharadas por cada 1 taza, así que 3 tazas son 3 grupos de 2 cucharadas. Halla ese total y colócalo en segundo lugar del par.

optional.stem: (Lesson 3.5) Chef Academy's snack bar sells 3 mini quiches for $6 or 5 mini quiches for $8. Which is the better deal per quiche?
optional.explanation: 3 for $6 is $6 / 3 = $2.00 per quiche. 5 for $8 is $8 / 5 = $1.60 per quiche. $1.60 < $2.00, so 5 quiches for $8 is the better deal.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. 3 for $6 is $6 / 3 = $2.00 per quiche.
The two prices do not reduce to the same cost per quiche. Divide each total by its number of quiches and compare.
Both prices and both counts are given, so a unit price can be calculated for each option.
optional.stemEs: La cafetería de la Academia de Chefs vende 3 mini quiches por $6 o 5 mini quiches por $8. ¿Cuál es la mejor oferta por quiche?
optional.explanationEs: 3 por $6 son $6 / 3 = $2.00 por quiche. 5 por $8 son $8 / 5 = $1.60 por quiche. Como $1.60 < $2.00, 5 quiches por $8 es la mejor oferta.
hints: A better deal means each single quiche costs less, not that the total price is smaller.
Find the unit price for each option: the total cost divided by the number of quiches.
The first option gives $6 ÷ 3 per quiche. Do the same division for $8 and 5 quiches, then compare the two prices.
hintsEs: Una mejor oferta significa que cada quiche cuesta menos, no que el precio total sea menor.
Encuentra el precio por unidad de cada opción: el costo total dividido entre la cantidad de quiches.
La primera opción da $6 ÷ 3 por quiche. Haz la misma división con $8 y 5 quiches y luego compara los dos precios.

optional.stem: (Lesson 3.6) Chef Reyes's pasta dough uses 2 eggs for every 3 cups of flour. For a banquet, the kitchen mixes 9 cups of flour. How many eggs are needed to keep the same ratio?
optional.explanation: Scale factor: 9 cups divided by 3 cups = 3. Multiply the eggs by the same factor: 2 x 3 = 6 eggs.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Scale factor: 9 cups divided by 3 cups = ___.
It looks like 6 was added to the 2 eggs. Ratios stay equal when both quantities are multiplied by the same factor, not when the same amount is added to each.
This doubles the eggs, but the flour did not double. Compare 9 cups to 3 cups to find the factor the recipe actually grew by.
optional.stemEs: La masa de pasta del chef Reyes usa 2 huevos por cada 3 tazas de harina. Para un banquete, la cocina mezcla 9 tazas de harina. ¿Cuántos huevos se necesitan para mantener la misma razón?
optional.explanationEs: Factor de escala: 9 tazas dividido entre 3 tazas = 3. Multiplica los huevos por el mismo factor: 2 x 3 = 6 huevos.
hints: Equivalent ratios keep the same relationship between eggs and flour, no matter how much dough you make.
Find the scale factor first: how many times larger is 9 cups than 3 cups?
The flour was multiplied by 3, so multiply the 2 eggs by 3 as well and see what you get.
hintsEs: Las razones equivalentes mantienen la misma relación entre huevos y harina, sin importar cuánta masa hagas.
Primero halla el factor de escala: ¿cuántas veces más grande es 9 tazas que 3 tazas?
La harina se multiplicó por 3, así que multiplica también los 2 huevos por 3 y observa qué obtienes.

optional.stem: (Lesson 3.7) In the kitchen, 3 pizzas feed exactly 12 people. At the same rate, how many pizzas are needed to feed 20 people?
optional.explanation: First find the unit rate: 12 people ÷ 3 pizzas = 4 people per pizza. Then 20 people ÷ 4 people per pizza = 5 pizzas.
choiceFeedback: Re-check how many times you need to multiply or scale.
That would feed more people than the problem asks about. Find how many people one pizza covers, then divide the 20 people by that number.
It looks like the people-per-pizza rate was flipped or skipped. Divide 12 by 3 to see what one pizza covers before dividing 20 by that rate.
optional.stemEs: En la cocina, 3 pizzas alcanzan exactamente para 12 personas. A la misma tasa, ¿cuántas pizzas se necesitan para alimentar a 20 personas?
optional.explanationEs: Primero halla la tasa por unidad: 12 personas ÷ 3 pizzas = 4 personas por pizza. Luego 20 personas ÷ 4 personas por pizza = 5 pizzas.
hints: A unit rate tells you how much one item is worth — here, how many people a single pizza feeds.
Find people per pizza first, then use that rate to see how many pizzas 20 people require.
12 people ÷ 3 pizzas gives 4 people per pizza. Now split the 20 people into groups of that size.
hintsEs: Una tasa por unidad te dice cuánto vale un solo elemento: aquí, para cuántas personas alcanza una pizza.
Halla primero las personas por pizza y luego usa esa tasa para ver cuántas pizzas necesitan 20 personas.
12 personas ÷ 3 pizzas da 4 personas por pizza. Ahora separa a las 20 personas en grupos de ese tamaño.

optional.stem: (Lesson 3.8) The snack bar compares two popcorn deals: 12 oz for $3.00 or 20 oz for $4.00. Which is the better buy?
choices: They cost the same per ounce
choiceFeedback: Find price per ounce for each.
Compare unit rates.
You have everything you need — each deal gives a total price and a total number of ounces, and that is enough to find a price per ounce.
optional.stemEs: El puesto de bocadillos compara dos ofertas de palomitas: 12 oz por $3.00 o 20 oz por $4.00. ¿Cuál es la mejor compra?
optional.explanationEs: 12 oz: $3.00 ÷ 12 = $0.25 por oz. 20 oz: $4.00 ÷ 20 = $0.20 por oz. $0.20 < $0.25, así que 20 oz por $4.00 es la mejor compra.
hints: Different package sizes can only be compared once both are priced per ounce.
Divide each deal's price by its number of ounces to get a cost per ounce.
Start with the 12-ounce deal: $3.00 ÷ 12. Then do the same for the 20-ounce deal and compare the two.
hintsEs: Los envases de distinto tamaño solo se pueden comparar cuando ambos tienen precio por onza.
Divide el precio de cada oferta entre su número de onzas para obtener el costo por onza.
Empieza con la oferta de 12 onzas: $3.00 ÷ 12. Luego haz lo mismo con la de 20 onzas y compara.

optional.stem: (Lesson 3.9) Chef Montoya's dressing uses 3 spoons of oil to 4 spoons of vinegar (3:4). Which recipe card shows an EQUIVALENT ratio?
optional.explanation: Multiply both parts of 3:4 by 3: 3 x 3 = 9 and 4 x 3 = 12, so 9:12 is equivalent to 3:4.
choiceFeedback: Scale both numbers by the same factor to make an equivalent ratio.
Only the vinegar was doubled while the oil stayed at 3, so the dressing would taste different. Both parts of a ratio have to be multiplied by the same number.
The same amount was added to each part, and adding does not preserve a ratio — it changes the relationship. Multiply both parts by the same factor instead.
optional.stemEs: El aderezo del chef Montoya usa 3 cucharadas de aceite por 4 cucharadas de vinagre (3:4). ¿Qué tarjeta de receta muestra una razón EQUIVALENTE?
optional.explanationEs: Multiplica ambas partes de 3:4 por 3: 3 × 3 = 9 y 4 × 3 = 12, así que 9:12 es equivalente a 3:4.
hints: Equivalent ratios describe the same relationship, so the dressing tastes the same even when the batch gets bigger.
Pick one multiplier and apply it to both the oil and the vinegar — never to just one of them.
Try tripling the recipe: 3 spoons of oil × 3 gives 9 spoons of oil. Now do the same to the 4 spoons of vinegar and see which card matches.
hintsEs: Las razones equivalentes describen la misma relación, así que el aderezo sabe igual aunque la preparación sea más grande.
Elige un multiplicador y aplícalo tanto al aceite como al vinagre, nunca a uno solo.
Prueba triplicar la receta: 3 cucharadas de aceite × 3 dan 9 cucharadas de aceite. Ahora haz lo mismo con las 4 cucharadas de vinagre y busca la tarjeta que coincida.

optional.stem: (Lesson 3.10) Leg 1: The joystick rod is 3 feet long, but the parts catalog lists it in inches. How many inches is that? (1 ft = 12 in)
optional.explanation: Inches are smaller than feet, so multiply: 3 × 12 = 36 inches.
choiceFeedback: Multiply by 12 (inches per foot).
How many inches per foot?
Check the conversion factor: a foot is 12 inches, not 11. Multiply the number of feet by 12.
optional.stemEs: Tramo 1: La barra de la palanca de mando mide 3 pies de largo, pero el catálogo de piezas la lista en pulgadas. ¿A cuántas pulgadas equivale? (1 pie = 12 pulgadas)
optional.explanationEs: Las pulgadas son más pequeñas que los pies, así que multiplica: 3 × 12 = 36 pulgadas.
hints: Converting to a smaller unit always produces a larger count of those units.
Decide whether to multiply or divide: inches are smaller than feet, so the number goes up.
Use the factor 1 ft = 12 in and set up 3 × 12. Finish that multiplication to get the length in inches.
hintsEs: Convertir a una unidad más pequeña siempre produce una cantidad mayor de esas unidades.
Decide si multiplicar o dividir: las pulgadas son más pequeñas que los pies, así que el número aumenta.
Usa el factor 1 pie = 12 pulgadas y plantea 3 × 12. Termina esa multiplicación para obtener la longitud en pulgadas.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 3.4) A ratio table shows (2, 6), (4, 12), and (6, 18). Which ordered pair comes next if the pattern continues?
approaching.explanation: The pattern adds 2 to x and 6 to y each time. After (6, 18): x = 6+2 = 8, y = 18+6 = 24. The next point is (8, 24).
choiceFeedback: Not quite. The pattern adds 2 to x and 6 to y each time.
Your x-value follows the pattern, but y only moved up 4. Look at how much y grows from one row to the next.
This jumps two steps in x while y only takes one. Each row moves x and y forward together, so check the step size for both.
hints: Watch each coordinate separately: x goes 2, 4, 6, … and y goes 6, 12, 18, …
Find the jump in the x-values and the jump in the y-values, then apply both jumps to (6, 18).
The x-values climb by 2, so add 2 to the 6 first. Then find the y-jump from 6 → 12 → 18 and add it to 18.
approaching.stemEs: Una tabla de razones muestra (2, 6), (4, 12) y (6, 18). ¿Cuál par ordenado sigue si el patrón continúa?
approaching.explanationEs: El patrón suma 2 a x y 6 a y cada vez. Después de (6, 18): x = 6+2 = 8, y = 18+6 = 24. El siguiente punto es (8, 24).
hintsEs: Observa cada coordenada por separado: x va 2, 4, 6, … y y va 6, 12, 18, …
Halla el salto de los valores de x y el salto de los valores de y, y luego aplica ambos saltos a (6, 18).
Los valores de x suben de 2 en 2, así que suma 2 al 6 primero. Luego halla el salto de y de 6 → 12 → 18 y súmalo a 18.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 3.4) When you graph equivalent ratios, the points will always form what shape?
choices: A straight line through the origin
approaching.explanation: Equivalent ratios are proportional, so their graph is always a straight line that passes through the origin (0, 0).
choiceFeedback: Re-check how many times you need to multiply or scale.
A zigzag would mean the ratio changes from point to point. Equivalent ratios grow by the same step every time, so the points stay in line.
A circle would bring the points back to where they started. Equivalent ratios keep climbing in one direction as x increases.
hints: Think about what happened when you plotted equivalent-ratio points earlier in this lesson.
Equivalent ratios grow steadily: every time x rises by the same amount, y rises by the same amount. What shape is steady growth?
Picture plotting (1, 2), (2, 4), (3, 6) and connecting them — and check whether (0, 0) would fit the pattern too.
approaching.stemEs: Cuando graficas razones equivalentes, ¿qué forma tomarán siempre los puntos?
approaching.explanationEs: Las razones equivalentes son proporcionales, así que su gráfica siempre es una línea recta que pasa por el origen (0, 0).
choicesEs: Una línea recta que pasa por el origen
hintsEs: Piensa en lo que pasó cuando graficaste puntos de razones equivalentes antes en esta lección.
Las razones equivalentes crecen de manera pareja: cada vez que x sube lo mismo, y sube lo mismo. ¿Qué forma tiene un crecimiento parejo?
Imagina graficar (1, 2), (2, 4), (3, 6) y unirlos, y revisa si (0, 0) también encajaría en el patrón.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 3.5) Chef A uses 2 cups of cheese for every 8 crackers. Chef B uses 3 cups of cheese for every 9 crackers. Who uses more cheese per cracker?
approaching.explanation: Chef A: 2÷8 = 0.25 cups per cracker. Chef B: 3÷9 ≈ 0.33 cups per cracker. Chef B uses more cheese per cracker.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Chef A: 2÷8 = ___ cups per cracker.
The two ratios do not reduce to the same value, so they are not equal. Divide each cheese amount by its cracker count and compare the results.
You have both amounts, so a comparison is possible. Turn each ratio into cheese per cracker and the answer appears.
hints: You can't compare 2 cups and 3 cups directly — the chefs use different numbers of crackers.
Find each chef's cheese for ONE cracker: divide cheese by crackers for each, then compare the two rates.
Chef A: divide 2 ÷ 8. Chef B: divide 3 ÷ 9. Compare those two decimals to see who uses more per cracker.
approaching.stemEs: El chef A usa 2 tazas de queso por cada 8 galletas saladas. El chef B usa 3 tazas de queso por cada 9 galletas saladas. ¿Quién usa más queso por galleta?
approaching.explanationEs: Chef A: 2÷8 = 0.25 tazas por galleta. Chef B: 3÷9 ≈ 0.33 tazas por galleta. El chef B usa más queso por galleta.
hintsEs: No puedes comparar 2 tazas y 3 tazas directamente: los chefs usan cantidades distintas de galletas.
Halla el queso de cada chef para UNA galleta: divide queso entre galletas en cada caso y luego compara las dos tasas.
Chef A: divide 2 ÷ 8. Chef B: divide 3 ÷ 9. Compara esos dos decimales para ver quién usa más por galleta.

approaching.explanation: Convert to the same denominator: 3:4 = 6:8. Since 6:8 > 5:8, the ratio 3:4 is greater.
choiceFeedback: Compare the ratios carefully — which one is greater?
Rewrite both ratios with the same second number before deciding. Scaling 3:4 so its second term is 8 makes the comparison direct.
Both ratios are exact numbers, so they can be compared. Scale one of them until the second terms match.
hints: The second numbers (4 and 8) don't match, so the ratios aren't ready to compare yet.
Rewrite the ratios with the same second number — 8 works nicely, since 4 × 2 = 8 — then compare the first numbers.
Scale 3:4 by 2: multiply both parts to get an out-of-8 ratio. Then compare its first number with the 5 in 5:8.
approaching.explanationEs: Convierte a un denominador común: 3:4 = 6:8. Como 6:8 > 5:8, la razón 3:4 es mayor.
hintsEs: Los segundos números (4 y 8) no coinciden, así que las razones todavía no están listas para compararse.
Reescribe las razones con el mismo segundo número —el 8 funciona bien, porque 4 × 2 = 8— y luego compara los primeros números.
Escala 3:4 por 2: multiplica ambas partes para obtener una razón sobre 8. Luego compara su primer número con el 5 de 5:8.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 3.6) A recipe uses 4 cups of broth for every 10 servings. How many cups of broth are needed for 30 servings?
approaching.explanation: Scale factor: 30 ÷ 10 = 3. Multiply broth by 3: 4 × 3 = 12 cups.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Scale factor: 30 ÷ 10 = ___.
That is 4 + 10, an adding move. Equivalent ratios are built by multiplying both quantities by the same factor, not by adding the same amount to each.
You multiplied 4 by 10, the number of servings in the recipe, instead of by the scale factor. First find how many times larger 30 servings is than 10 servings.
hints: The servings jumped from 10 to 30 — the broth must grow by the same factor.
Find the scale factor by dividing the new servings by the recipe's servings, then multiply the broth by it.
Divide 30 ÷ 10 to get the scale factor — then multiply 4 cups of broth by that number.
approaching.stemEs: Una receta usa 4 tazas de caldo por cada 10 porciones. ¿Cuántas tazas de caldo se necesitan para 30 porciones?
approaching.explanationEs: Factor de escala: 30 ÷ 10 = 3. Multiplica el caldo por 3: 4 × 3 = 12 tazas.
hintsEs: Las porciones pasaron de 10 a 30: el caldo debe crecer con el mismo factor.
Halla el factor de escala dividiendo las porciones nuevas entre las de la receta y luego multiplica el caldo por él.
Divide 30 ÷ 10 para obtener el factor de escala y luego multiplica las 4 tazas de caldo por ese número.

approaching.explanation: Divide 6:9 by 3 to get 2:3. Since both ratios simplify to 2:3, they are equivalent.
choiceFeedback: Scale both numbers by the same factor to make an equivalent ratio.
Not quite. Since both ratios simplify to 2:3, they are equivalent.
Subtracting the two parts is not the test for equivalent ratios. Two ratios are equivalent when one can be multiplied or divided by the same number to become the other.
hints: Two ratios are equivalent when one simplifies (or scales) exactly into the other.
Try dividing both parts of 6:9 by the same number — adding or subtracting the parts proves nothing about ratios.
Divide the 6 by 3 and the 9 by 3, then compare what you get with 2:3.
approaching.explanationEs: Divide 6:9 entre 3 para obtener 2:3. Como ambas razones se simplifican a 2:3, son equivalentes.
choicesEs: Sí, las dos se simplifican a 2:3
hintsEs: Dos razones son equivalentes cuando una se simplifica (o se escala) exactamente hasta la otra.
Prueba dividir ambas partes de 6:9 entre el mismo número; sumar o restar las partes no prueba nada sobre razones.
Divide el 6 entre 3 y el 9 entre 3, y luego compara lo que obtengas con 2:3.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 3.7) A bakery makes 24 cookies in 3 batches. What is the unit rate of cookies per batch?
approaching.explanation: Unit rate: 24 cookies ÷ 3 batches = 8 cookies per batch.
choiceFeedback: Re-check how many times you need to multiply or scale.
That is the total number of cookies from all the batches together, not the amount in one batch. A unit rate always describes a single batch, so divide the total by 3.
It looks like the division came out short. Split 24 cookies evenly among the 3 batches again and count how many land in one batch.
hints: 'Per batch' means the number of cookies in exactly ONE batch.
Divide the total cookies by the number of batches to find one batch's share.
Divide 24 cookies by 3 batches — the quotient is your cookies per batch.
approaching.stemEs: Una panadería hace 24 galletas en 3 tandas. ¿Cuál es la tasa por unidad de galletas por tanda?
approaching.explanationEs: Tasa por unidad: 24 galletas ÷ 3 tandas = 8 galletas por tanda.
hintsEs: 'Por tanda' significa el número de galletas de exactamente UNA tanda.
Divide el total de galletas entre el número de tandas para hallar lo que le toca a una tanda.
Divide 24 galletas entre 3 tandas: el cociente son tus galletas por tanda.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 3.7) Apples cost $5 for 4 pounds. What is the cost per pound?
choiceFeedback: That is what you get if you divided 4 by 5. Instead: Unit rate: $5 ÷ 4 pounds = $1.25 per pound.
That price does not come from dividing $5 by 4 pounds. Carry out the division to the exact cents instead of rounding to a friendly number.
That number is the pound count, not a price. Cost per pound comes from dividing the dollars by the pounds.
hints: 'Cost per pound' asks for the dollars for exactly ONE pound.
Divide the total price by the number of pounds. Keep the money on top: dollars ÷ pounds.
Divide 5 ÷ 4 — writing it as 5.00 ÷ 4 can make the decimal easier to see.
approaching.stemEs: Las manzanas cuestan $5 por 4 libras. ¿Cuál es el costo por libra?
approaching.explanationEs: Tasa por unidad: $5 ÷ 4 libras = $1.25 por libra.
hintsEs: 'Costo por libra' pide los dólares de exactamente UNA libra.
Divide el precio total entre el número de libras. Deja el dinero arriba: dólares ÷ libras.
Divide 5 ÷ 4; escribirlo como 5.00 ÷ 4 puede facilitar ver el decimal.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 3.8) Which is the better buy: 6 bouncy balls for $4.50 or 10 bouncy balls for $8.00?
choices: They cost the same per ball
choiceFeedback: Find the price per ball for each: divide cost by quantity.
Compare the unit prices.
Make sure you're dividing cost by quantity for each option.
hints: You can't compare $4.50 and $8.00 straight across — the packs hold different numbers of balls.
Find each pack's price for ONE ball (cost ÷ number of balls), then compare the two unit prices.
Start with the first deal: $4.50 ÷ 6. Then compute $8.00 ÷ 10 and see which per-ball price is lower.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál es la mejor compra: 6 pelotas saltarinas por $4.50 o 10 pelotas saltarinas por $8.00?
approaching.explanationEs: $4.50 ÷ 6 = $0.75 cada una. $8.00 ÷ 10 = $0.80 cada una. $0.75 < $0.80, así que 6 por $4.50 es la mejor compra.
hintsEs: No puedes comparar $4.50 y $8.00 directamente: los paquetes traen cantidades distintas de pelotas.
Halla el precio de UNA pelota en cada paquete (costo ÷ número de pelotas) y luego compara los dos precios unitarios.
Empieza con la primera oferta: $4.50 ÷ 6. Luego calcula $8.00 ÷ 10 y ve qué precio por pelota es menor.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 3.8) A faucet drips 15 ounces of water in 5 minutes. What is the unit rate?
choiceFeedback: Divide: 15 ounces ÷ 5 minutes.
Find the rate per minute.
You divided the minutes by the ounces. For ounces per minute, ounces go first.
hints: The unit rate here is ounces per ONE minute — 15 ounces spread across 5 minutes.
Divide the ounces by the minutes so the time becomes 1 minute.
Set up 15 ÷ 5 ounces per minute.
approaching.stemEs: Una llave gotea 15 onzas de agua en 5 minutos. ¿Cuál es la tasa por unidad?
hintsEs: La tasa unitaria aquí son onzas por UN minuto: 15 onzas repartidas en 5 minutos.
Divide las onzas entre los minutos para que el tiempo se vuelva 1 minuto.
Plantea 15 ÷ 5 onzas por minuto.

approaching.explanation: Multiply both parts by 2: 2×2 = 4 and 5×2 = 10, so 4:10 is equivalent to 2:5.
choiceFeedback: Scale both numbers by the same factor to make an equivalent ratio.
Only the second number was multiplied here — the first part stayed at 2. In equivalent ratios both parts must be multiplied by the same factor.
Those are the right two numbers, but the order got flipped. A ratio compares the first quantity to the second, so the order has to stay the same.
hints: Equivalent ratios come from multiplying BOTH parts of 2:5 by the same number.
For each choice, ask: what did the 2 become, and what did the 5 become? Both must be multiplied by the same amount.
Try multiplying both parts of 2:5 by 2 and see what ratio appears. Then look for that pattern among the choices.
approaching.explanationEs: Multiplica ambas partes por 2: 2×2 = 4 y 5×2 = 10, así que 4:10 es equivalente a 2:5.
hintsEs: Las razones equivalentes salen de multiplicar AMBAS partes de 2:5 por el mismo número.
Para cada opción pregunta: ¿en qué se convirtió el 2 y en qué se convirtió el 5? Ambos deben multiplicarse por la misma cantidad.
Prueba multiplicar ambas partes de 2:5 por 2 y mira qué razón aparece. Luego busca ese patrón entre las opciones.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 3.9) A recipe uses 4 eggs for every 6 cups of flour. Which ratio is equivalent?
approaching.explanation: Divide both by 2: 4÷2 = 2 and 6÷2 = 3. The ratio 2:3 is equivalent to 4:6.
choiceFeedback: Scale both numbers by the same factor to make an equivalent ratio.
The flour amount was divided but the eggs stayed the same. Divide both parts of the ratio by the same number to keep it equivalent.
These are the original numbers with the order swapped. Keep eggs first and flour second, then scale both parts the same way.
hints: You can scale a ratio DOWN too — divide both parts by the same number.
Look for a number that divides evenly into both 4 and 6, then divide each part by it.
Both 4 and 6 are even, so divide each by 2 and see what simpler ratio you get.
approaching.stemEs: Una receta usa 4 huevos por cada 6 tazas de harina. ¿Qué razón es equivalente?
approaching.explanationEs: Divide ambas partes entre 2: 4÷2 = 2 y 6÷2 = 3. La razón 2:3 es equivalente a 4:6.
hintsEs: También puedes escalar una razón HACIA ABAJO: divide ambas partes entre el mismo número.
Busca un número que divida exacto tanto al 4 como al 6 y luego divide cada parte entre él.
Tanto 4 como 6 son pares, así que divide cada uno entre 2 y mira qué razón más simple obtienes.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 3.10) How many inches are in 7 feet?
choiceFeedback: Multiply 7 by 12 (inches per foot).
There are 12 inches in every foot.
You multiplied by 8 feet. Re-read how many feet the question gives.
hints: The key fact: 1 foot = 12 inches. You have 7 feet and want inches.
Going from a BIGGER unit (feet) to a SMALLER unit (inches) means you multiply.
Set up 7 × 12 — seven groups of 12 inches.
hintsEs: El dato clave: 1 pie = 12 pulgadas. Tienes 7 pies y quieres pulgadas.
Ir de una unidad MAYOR (pies) a una MENOR (pulgadas) significa que multiplicas.
Plantea 7 × 12: siete grupos de 12 pulgadas.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 3.10) How many feet are in 3 yards?
choiceFeedback: Multiply 3 by 3 (feet per yard).
There are 3 feet in every yard.
Not quite. 1 yard = ___ feet.
hints: The key fact: 1 yard = 3 feet. You have 3 yards and want feet.
Big unit (yards) to small unit (feet) means multiply by the conversion factor 3.
Set up 3 × 3 — three yards, each worth 3 feet.
hintsEs: El dato clave: 1 yarda = 3 pies. Tienes 3 yardas y quieres pies.
De unidad grande (yardas) a unidad pequeña (pies) significa multiplicar por el factor de conversión 3.
Plantea 3 × 3: tres yardas, cada una de 3 pies.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 3.4) Points from a ratio table are plotted at (1, 4), (2, 8), and (3, 12). What is the ratio of y to x for each point?
onLevel.explanation: For each point: 4÷1 = 4, 8÷2 = 4, 12÷3 = 4. The ratio of y to x is always 4:1.
choiceFeedback: That is what you get if you wrote the two quantities in the reverse order. Instead: The ratio of y to x is always 4:1 — the y-value divided by the x-value.
Those numbers do come from the table, but they are written x to y and left unsimplified. Divide y by x and reduce.
This mixes numbers from two different points. Pair each point's own y with its own x, then simplify.
hints: The question asks y to x — the up-value compared to the across-value, in that order.
Divide y by x for each point. Equivalent ratios should give the same result all three times.
Take (2, 8): divide 8 ÷ 2. Check that (1, 4) and (3, 12) give the same value, then write it as y first, x second.
onLevel.stemEs: Los puntos de una tabla de razones se grafican en (1, 4), (2, 8) y (3, 12). ¿Cuál es la razón de y a x en cada punto?
onLevel.explanationEs: Para cada punto: 4÷1 = 4, 8÷2 = 4, 12÷3 = 4. La razón de y a x siempre es 4:1.
hintsEs: La pregunta pide y a x: el valor vertical comparado con el horizontal, en ese orden.
Divide y entre x en cada punto. Las razones equivalentes deben dar el mismo resultado las tres veces.
Toma (2, 8): divide 8 ÷ 2. Comprueba que (1, 4) y (3, 12) den el mismo valor y luego escríbelo con y primero y x después.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 3.4) Two students graph ratio tables. Student A plots (1,2), (2,4), (3,6). Student B plots (1,3), (2,6), (3,9). Whose line is steeper?
onLevel.explanation: Student A's ratio is 1:2 (y goes up 2 for each 1 in x). Student B's ratio is 1:3 (y goes up 3 for each 1 in x). A higher rate of change means a steeper line, so Student B's is steeper.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Student A's ratio is 1:2 (y goes up 2 for each 1 in x).
Both lines do rise, but not at the same rate. Compare how far y climbs for each single step in x.
You actually have enough information — every point gives a unit rate. Divide y by x for one point in each set and compare the two.
hints: Steepness comes from how fast y climbs each time x grows by 1 — not from who has bigger points overall.
Find each student's rate: divide y by x for one of their points. The bigger rate makes the steeper line.
Student A's line rises 2 for each 1 in x (see (1, 2)). Find Student B's rise from (1, 3), then compare the two rates.
onLevel.stemEs: Dos estudiantes grafican tablas de razones. El estudiante A grafica (1,2), (2,4), (3,6). El estudiante B grafica (1,3), (2,6), (3,9). ¿Cuál línea es más inclinada?
onLevel.explanationEs: La razón del estudiante A es 1:2 (y sube 2 por cada 1 de x). La razón del estudiante B es 1:3 (y sube 3 por cada 1 de x). Una tasa de cambio mayor significa una línea más inclinada, así que la del estudiante B es más inclinada.
hintsEs: Lo empinado depende de qué tan rápido sube y cada vez que x crece 1, no de quién tiene los puntos más grandes en general.
Halla la razón de cada estudiante: divide y entre x en uno de sus puntos. La razón mayor da la recta más empinada.
La recta del Estudiante A sube 2 por cada 1 de x (mira (1, 2)). Halla la subida del Estudiante B con (1, 3) y compara las dos razones.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 3.5) Store A sells 3 mangoes for $6. Store B sells 5 mangoes for $9. Which store offers a better price per mango?
onLevel.explanation: Store A: $6÷3 = $2.00 per mango. Store B: $9÷5 = $1.80 per mango. Store B has the better (lower) price per mango.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Store A: $6÷3 = $2.00 per mango.
$6 for 3 and $9 for 5 do not give the same unit price. Divide each total by its number of mangoes to check.
Both the prices and the counts are known, so a unit price can be found for each store.
hints: The stores sell different counts for different prices — compare the price of ONE mango.
Divide dollars by mangoes for each store, then choose the store with the lower per-mango price.
Store A: divide 6 ÷ 3 for its price per mango. Store B: divide 9 ÷ 5. Compare the two prices.
onLevel.stemEs: La tienda A vende 3 mangos por $6. La tienda B vende 5 mangos por $9. ¿Cuál tienda ofrece mejor precio por mango?
onLevel.explanationEs: Tienda A: $6÷3 = $2.00 por mango. Tienda B: $9÷5 = $1.80 por mango. La tienda B tiene el mejor precio (el más bajo) por mango.
hintsEs: Las tiendas venden cantidades distintas a precios distintos: compara el precio de UN mango.
Divide dólares entre mangos en cada tienda y luego elige la tienda con el menor precio por mango.
Tienda A: divide 6 ÷ 3 para su precio por mango. Tienda B: divide 9 ÷ 5. Compara los dos precios.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 3.5) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the problem
workedExample.work: Compare Chef Reyes's dressing (4 tbsp oil : 6 tbsp vinegar) to Chef Tran's dressing (5 tbsp oil : 8 tbsp vinegar). Which dressing is oilier?
workedExample.workEs: Compara el aderezo del chef Reyes (4 cdas de aceite : 6 cdas de vinagre) con el del chef Tran (5 cdas de aceite : 8 cdas de vinagre). ¿Cuál aderezo tiene más aceite?

workedExample.label: Find a common denominator
workedExample.workEs: El mínimo común denominador de 6 y 8 es 24.

workedExample.label: Scale each ratio
workedExample.work: Chef Reyes: 6 × 4 = 24, so oil = 4 × 4 = 16, giving 16:24. Chef Tran: to reach 24 he also multiplies by 4: oil = 5 × 4 = 20, giving 20:24.
workedExample.workEs: Chef Reyes: 6 × 4 = 24, así que aceite = 4 × 4 = 16, lo que da 16:24. Chef Tran: para llegar a 24 también multiplica por 4: aceite = 5 × 4 = 20, lo que da 20:24.

workedExample.label: Conclusion
workedExample.work: Since 20 > 16, Chef Tran's dressing is oilier.
workedExample.workEs: Como 20 > 16, el aderezo del chef Tran tiene más aceite.

onLevel.correctWork: Each ratio needs its own multiplier to reach 24 — Chef Reyes and Chef Tran do not use the same multiplier. Chef Tran's vinegar is 8, and 8 × 3 = 24 (not 8 × 4 = 32), so multiply BOTH parts of his ratio by 3, not 4: oil = 5 × 3 = 15, giving 15:24. Now compare with equal vinegar (24): Chef Reyes has 16 tbsp oil and Chef Tran has 15 tbsp oil. Since 16 > 15, Chef Reyes's dressing is actually oilier.
hints: Look at Step 3. Each ratio needs its own multiplier to reach the common denominator (24) — Chef Reyes and Chef Tran do not need the same multiplier.
8 × 3 = 24, so what should you multiply BOTH parts of Chef Tran's ratio by?
onLevel.explanation: Each ratio needs its own multiplier to reach 24. Chef Reyes's vinegar 6 × 4 = 24 is right, but Chef Tran's vinegar is 8, and 8 × 3 = 24, so both parts of his ratio scale by 3: 5 × 3 = 15, giving 15:24 instead of 20:24. Compared at equal vinegar, 16 tbsp of oil beats 15, so Chef Reyes's dressing is the oilier one.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada razón necesita su propio multiplicador para llegar a 24. El vinagre del chef Reyes, 6 × 4 = 24, está bien, pero el vinagre del chef Tran es 8, y 8 × 3 = 24, así que las dos partes de su razón se multiplican por 3: 5 × 3 = 15, lo que da 15:24 en vez de 20:24. Comparados con el mismo vinagre, 16 cucharadas de aceite superan a 15, así que el aderezo del chef Reyes es el más aceitoso.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Cada razón necesita su propio multiplicador para llegar a 24 — el chef Reyes y el chef Tran no usan el mismo. El vinagre del chef Tran es 8, y 8 × 3 = 24 (no 8 × 4 = 32), así que multiplica AMBAS partes de su razón por 3, no por 4: aceite = 5 × 3 = 15, lo que da 15:24. Ahora compara con vinagre igual (24): el chef Reyes tiene 16 cdas de aceite y el chef Tran tiene 15 cdas. Como 16 > 15, el aderezo del chef Reyes en realidad tiene más aceite.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 3.6) A chef uses the proportion 3/7 = x/28 to scale a recipe. What is x?
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Scale factor: 28 ÷ 7 = ___.
This uses a scale factor of 3, but the denominator did not triple. Divide 28 by 7 to see how many times larger the new denominator really is.
21 is 28 − 7, a subtracting move. Proportions grow by multiplying both parts by the same factor.
hints: Look at the bottoms of the fractions first: the 7 became 28.
Divide 28 by 7 to find the scale factor, then multiply the top number 3 by that same factor.
Compute 28 ÷ 7, then multiply 3 by the result to get x.
onLevel.stemEs: Un chef usa la proporción 3/7 = x/28 para ajustar una receta. ¿Cuánto vale x?
onLevel.explanationEs: Factor de escala: 28 ÷ 7 = 4. Multiplica: 3 × 4 = 12. Entonces x = 12.
hintsEs: Mira primero la parte de abajo de las fracciones: el 7 se volvió 28.
Divide 28 entre 7 para hallar el factor de escala y luego multiplica el número de arriba, 3, por ese mismo factor.
Calcula 28 ÷ 7 y luego multiplica 3 por el resultado para obtener x.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 3.6) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Set up the proportion
workedExample.work: A recipe uses 4 cups of sugar for every 9 cups of flour: 4/9 = x/27.
workedExample.workEs: Una receta usa 4 tazas de azúcar por cada 9 tazas de harina: 4/9 = x/27.

workedExample.label: Solve for x
workedExample.workEs: 4 + 3 = 7, así que x = 7 tazas de azúcar.

onLevel.correctWork: Multiply by the scale factor instead of adding it: 4 × 3 = 12 cups of sugar. To keep ratios equivalent you multiply both parts by the scale factor — you never add it.
hints: Look at Step 3. The scale factor of 3 is correct, but what operation should you use with it?
To scale a ratio you MULTIPLY both parts by the factor (4 × 3), you do not add (4 + 3).
onLevel.explanation: The solving step added the scale factor instead of multiplying by it. Because 27 is 9 × 3, the sugar has to grow the same way: 4 × 3 = 12 cups. Adding would break the relationship, since 7/27 is not equivalent to 4/9 but 12/27 is.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso de resolver sumó el factor de escala en vez de multiplicar por él. Como 27 es 9 × 3, el azúcar tiene que crecer igual: 4 × 3 = 12 tazas. Sumar rompería la relación, porque 7/27 no es equivalente a 4/9, pero 12/27 sí lo es.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Multiplica por el factor de escala en lugar de sumarlo: 4 × 3 = 12 tazas de azúcar. Para mantener razones equivalentes multiplicas ambas partes por el factor de escala — nunca lo sumas.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 3.7) A car travels 150 miles in 3 hours. A bus travels 200 miles in 5 hours. Which vehicle is faster?
onLevel.explanation: Car: 150÷3 = 50 mph. Bus: 200÷5 = 40 mph. The car travels faster at 50 mph vs. 40 mph.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Car: 150÷3 = ___ mph.
The distances and the times are both different, so equal speed cannot be assumed. Divide each distance by its own time and compare the two unit rates.
There is enough information here — each vehicle gives both a distance and a time. Turn each pair into miles per hour and the comparison becomes clear.
hints: You can't compare 150 miles and 200 miles directly — the travel times are different.
Find each vehicle's speed in miles per ONE hour: divide miles by hours, then compare the two speeds.
Car: divide 150 ÷ 3. Bus: divide 200 ÷ 5. The bigger miles-per-hour value belongs to the faster vehicle.
onLevel.stemEs: Un carro recorre 150 millas en 3 horas. Un autobús recorre 200 millas en 5 horas. ¿Cuál vehículo es más rápido?
onLevel.explanationEs: Carro: 150 ÷ 3 = 50 mph. Autobús: 200 ÷ 5 = 40 mph. El carro va más rápido, a 50 mph frente a 40 mph.
hintsEs: No puedes comparar 150 millas y 200 millas directamente: los tiempos de viaje son distintos.
Halla la velocidad de cada vehículo en millas por UNA hora: divide millas entre horas y luego compara las dos velocidades.
Carro: divide 150 ÷ 3. Autobús: divide 200 ÷ 5. El valor mayor de millas por hora es del vehículo más rápido.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 3.7) Spot the Smoothie Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the problem
workedExample.work: A smoothie stand makes 18 smoothies in 6 minutes. How many smoothies can it make in 10 minutes at the same rate?
workedExample.workEs: Un puesto de licuados prepara 18 licuados en 6 minutos. ¿Cuántos licuados puede preparar en 10 minutos a la misma tasa?

workedExample.label: Find the unit rate
workedExample.workEs: 6 minutos ÷ 18 licuados = 0.33 de minuto por licuado

onLevel.correctWork: The unit rate was divided in the wrong order. The question asks for smoothies, so find smoothies per minute: 18 smoothies ÷ 6 minutes = 3 smoothies per minute. Then 3 × 10 = 30 smoothies in 10 minutes.
hints: Look at Step 2. The question asks how many smoothies, so the unit rate should be smoothies per minute, not minutes per smoothie.
Divide 18 smoothies by 6 minutes to get 3 smoothies per minute, then multiply by 10 minutes to get 30 smoothies.
onLevel.explanation: The unit rate step divides 6 minutes by 18 smoothies, which answers 'how long per smoothie' when the question asks how many smoothies. Put the quantity you want on top: 18 ÷ 6 = 3 smoothies per minute, so 3 × 10 = 30 smoothies in 10 minutes.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso de la tasa por unidad divide 6 minutos entre 18 batidos, lo cual responde «cuánto tiempo por batido» cuando la pregunta es cuántos batidos. Coloca arriba la cantidad que buscas: 18 ÷ 6 = 3 batidos por minuto, así que 3 × 10 = 30 batidos en 10 minutos.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: La tasa unitaria se dividió en el orden equivocado. La pregunta pide licuados, así que encuentra licuados por minuto: 18 licuados ÷ 6 minutos = 3 licuados por minuto. Luego 3 × 10 = 30 licuados en 10 minutos.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 3.8) A machine dispenses 24 tokens in 3 minutes. At this rate, how many tokens does it dispense in 10 minutes?
onLevel.explanation: Unit rate: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 tokens per minute. In 10 minutes: 8 × 10 = 80 tokens.
choiceFeedback: First find tokens per minute: 24 ÷ 3. Then multiply by 12 minutes.
Find the unit rate, then use it to find the answer for 12 minutes.
You need to find how many tokens per minute first.
hints: Two steps: find tokens per ONE minute first, then stretch that rate to 10 minutes.
Divide tokens by minutes for the unit rate, then multiply the rate by the new time.
Step 1: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 tokens each minute. Step 2: multiply that rate by 10 minutes.
onLevel.stemEs: Una máquina despacha 24 fichas en 3 minutos. A ese ritmo, ¿cuántas fichas despacha en 10 minutos?
onLevel.explanationEs: Tasa por unidad: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 fichas por minuto. En 10 minutos: 8 × 10 = 80 fichas.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 3.8) A factory produces 360 widgets in 8 hours. At the same rate, how many widgets are produced in a 12-hour shift?
onLevel.explanation: Unit rate: 360 ÷ 8 = 45 widgets per hour. In 12 hours: 45 × 12 = 540 widgets.
choiceFeedback: First find widgets per hour: 360 ÷ 8. Then multiply by 20 hours.
Find the unit rate, then use it to find the answer for 20 hours.
Start by finding how many widgets per hour.
hints: Two steps: find widgets per ONE hour first, then scale up to the 12-hour shift.
Divide widgets by hours for the unit rate, then multiply that rate by 12.
Step 1: 360 ÷ 8 = 45 widgets each hour. Step 2: multiply that rate by 12 hours.
onLevel.stemEs: Una fábrica produce 360 piezas en 8 horas. Al mismo ritmo, ¿cuántas piezas se producen en un turno de 12 horas?
onLevel.explanationEs: Tasa por unidad: 360 ÷ 8 = 45 piezas por hora. En 12 horas: 45 × 12 = 540 piezas.
hintsEs: Dos pasos: halla primero los artículos por UNA hora y luego escálalo al turno de 12 horas.
Divide los artículos entre las horas para la tasa unitaria y luego multiplica esa tasa por 12.
Paso 1: 360 ÷ 8 = 45 artículos por hora. Paso 2: multiplica esa tasa por 12 horas.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 3.9) Marcus earns $45 for every 3 hours of work. How much does he earn in 8 hours?
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Unit rate: $45 ÷ 3 = $15/hour.
That is what Marcus would earn for 9 hours, not 8. Find the pay for a single hour first, then multiply by the number of hours the question asks about.
It looks like extra hours were added on top of the original $45 instead of scaling the whole rate. Divide to get the pay for one hour, then multiply by all 8 hours.
hints: 8 hours is not a whole-number multiple of 3 hours, so find what Marcus earns in ONE hour first.
Unit rate: divide the $45 by the 3 hours, then multiply that hourly pay by 8 hours.
Divide 45 ÷ 3 to get dollars per hour — then multiply that rate by 8.
onLevel.stemEs: Marcus gana $45 por cada 3 horas de trabajo. ¿Cuánto gana en 8 horas?
onLevel.explanationEs: Tasa por unidad: $45 ÷ 3 = $15 por hora. En 8 horas: $15 × 8 = $120.
hintsEs: 8 horas no es un múltiplo entero de 3 horas, así que primero halla cuánto gana Marcus en UNA hora.
Tasa unitaria: divide los $45 entre las 3 horas y luego multiplica ese pago por hora por 8 horas.
Divide 45 ÷ 3 para obtener los dólares por hora y luego multiplica esa tasa por 8.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 3.9) Spot the Common Mistake — Simplifying a Ratio

workedExample.label: Set up the ratio
workedExample.work: A student wants to write 12:18 in simplest form.
workedExample.workEs: Un estudiante quiere escribir 12:18 en su forma más simple.

workedExample.label: Find the common factor
workedExample.work: Both 12 and 18 can be divided by 6.
workedExample.workEs: Tanto 12 como 18 se pueden dividir entre 6.

onLevel.correctWork: Divide BOTH parts by the same number: 12 ÷ 6 = 2 and 18 ÷ 6 = 3, so 12:18 simplifies to 2:3.
hints: Look at Step 3. They divided 12 by 6 but divided 18 by 3 — those are different numbers.
To keep ratios equivalent, divide both numbers by the SAME amount. 12:18 divided by 6 each gives 2:3.
onLevel.titleEs: Encuentra el error común — Simplificar una razón
onLevel.explanation: The "Divide each part" step uses two different divisors: 12 ÷ 6 but 18 ÷ 3. Simplifying only keeps a ratio equivalent when both parts are divided by the same number, so 12 ÷ 6 = 2 and 18 ÷ 6 = 3 give 2:3. The student's 2:6 simplifies to 1:3, which is not the same comparison as 12:18.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso "Divide each part" usa dos divisores distintos: 12 ÷ 6 pero 18 ÷ 3. workedExample.label: Convert 80 ounces of bolts to pounds

onLevel.correctWork: Ounces are smaller than pounds, so you divide (not multiply): 80 ÷ 16 = 5 pounds. Changing to a bigger unit gives a smaller number.
hints: You are going from a smaller unit (ounces) to a larger unit (pounds). Should the number get bigger or smaller?
Changing to a larger unit means fewer of them, so divide: 80 ÷ 16 = 5 pounds.
onLevel.explanation: The Operate step multiplied when it should have divided. Pounds are bigger than ounces, so the 80 ounces bundle into 80 ÷ 16 = 5 pounds. An answer of 1,280 pounds should stand out immediately — a container of bolts that weighs 80 ounces is only about 5 pounds.
onLevel.explanationEs: En el paso de operar se multiplicó cuando había que dividir. Las libras son más grandes que las onzas, así que las 80 onzas se agrupan en 80 ÷ 16 = 5 libras. Una respuesta de 1,280 libras debería llamar la atención de inmediato: un recipiente de tornillos que pesa 80 onzas pesa apenas unas 5 libras.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Las onzas son más pequeñas que las libras, así que se divide (no se multiplica): 80 ÷ 16 = 5 libras. Cambiar a una unidad más grande da un número más pequeño.

extending.title: (Lesson 3.4) Find Jada's Mistake

extending.explanationEs: Jada escribió primero el valor de la leche, así que sus pares quedaron (1, 2), (2, 4), (3, 6). Su propia conclusión dice que las galletas van en el eje x, así que el valor de las galletas debe ir primero: los pares son (2, 1), (4, 2) y (6, 3).
extending.correctWorkEs: Los pares ordenados deben ser (2, 1), (4, 2), (6, 3) — las galletas van en x y la leche en y, siguiendo el orden de las columnas de la tabla.

extending.title: (Lesson 3.5) Find Kai's Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the problem
workedExample.work: Compare 3:5 and 4:7. Which ratio is greater?

workedExample.label: Find common denominator
workedExample.workEs: El mínimo común denominador de 5 y 7 es 35

workedExample.label: Scale the ratios
workedExample.work: 3:5 = 21:35 (3 × 7 = 21). For 4:7, Kai multiplies by 7 again: 4 × 7 = 28, giving 28:35.
workedExample.workEs: 3:5 = 21:35 (3 × 7 = 21). Para 4:7, Kai multiplica por 7 otra vez: 4 × 7 = 28, lo que da 28:35.

extending.correctWork: To scale 4:7 to 35ths, multiply by 35 ÷ 7 = 5, not by 7 again: 4 × 5 = 20, so 4:7 = 20:35 (not 28:35). Now compare correctly: 21:35 vs. 20:35. Since 21 > 20, the ratio 3:5 is actually greater, not 4:7.
hints: Look at Step 3. To turn 7 into 35, Kai should multiply by 35 ÷ 7 = 5 — but he used 7 again, the denominator from the OTHER ratio.
Find the correct multiplier for 4:7 (35 ÷ 7), then multiply BOTH the 4 and the 7 by that number.
extending.explanation: Kai reused the multiplier 7 that belonged to the first ratio instead of finding the one 4:7 actually needs. To reach 35ths you multiply by 35 ÷ 7 = 5, so 4:7 = 20:35, not 28:35. Comparing 21:35 with 20:35 shows 3:5 is the greater ratio — the opposite of the conclusion.
extending.explanationEs: Kai reutilizó el multiplicador 7, que pertenecía a la primera razón, en vez de buscar el que realmente necesita 4:7. Para llegar a treinta y cincoavos se multiplica por 35 ÷ 7 = 5, así que 4:7 = 20:35, no 28:35. Al comparar 21:35 con 20:35 se ve que 3:5 es la razón mayor, lo contrario de la conclusión.
extending.correctWorkEs: Para escalar 4:7 a 35avos, multiplica por 35 ÷ 7 = 5, no por 7 otra vez: 4 × 5 = 20, así que 4:7 = 20:35 (no 28:35). Ahora compara bien: 21:35 vs. 20:35. Como 21 > 20, la razón 3:5 es en realidad la mayor, no 4:7.

extending.title: (Lesson 3.6) Find Priya's Mistake
extending.correctWork: 5 × 4 = 20 (multiply by the scale factor, don't add it)
hints: Look at Step 3. Priya found the correct scale factor of 4, but what did she do with it?
To keep ratios equivalent, multiply both parts by the scale factor — do NOT add.
extending.explanation: In the solving step Priya added the scale factor to 5 instead of multiplying by it. Since 32 is 8 × 4, the top of the fraction scales the same way: 5 × 4 = 20, so x = 20 and 20/32 simplifies right back to 5/8.
extending.explanationEs: En el paso de resolver, Priya sumó el factor de escala a 5 en vez de multiplicar por él. Como 32 es 8 × 4, la parte de arriba de la fracción se escala igual: 5 × 4 = 20, así que x = 20 y 20/32 se simplifica de nuevo a 5/8.
extending.correctWorkEs: 5 × 4 = 20 (multiplica por el factor de escala, no lo sumes)

workedExample.label: Read the problem

hints: Look at Step 3. Mia found the correct unit rate of $0.75, but what did she do with it?
To find the total cost, you multiply the unit rate by the number of items — not add.
extending.explanation: Mia's unit rate $4.50 ÷ 6 = $0.75 per orange is correct, but she then wrote $0.75 + 10 instead of multiplying. Ten oranges at $0.75 each cost $0.75 × 10 = $7.50.
extending.explanationEs: La tasa por unidad de Mía, $4.50 ÷ 6 = $0.75 por naranja, está correcta, pero luego escribió $0.75 + 10 en lugar de multiplicar. Diez naranjas a $0.75 cada una cuestan $0.75 × 10 = $7.50.
extending.correctWorkEs: $0.75 × 10 = $7.50 (multiplica la tasa unitaria, no la sumes)

extending.title: (Lesson 3.8) Find the Unit Rate Error

workedExample.label: Which is the better buy: 5 lb for $8.75 or 3 lb for $5.10?
workedExample.labelEs: ¿Cuál es la mejor compra: 5 lb por $8.75 o 3 lb por $5.10?

workedExample.label: Find unit rate for Deal 1
workedExample.labelEs: Encuentra la tasa unitaria de la oferta 1

workedExample.label: Find unit rate for Deal 2
workedExample.labelEs: Encuentra la tasa unitaria de la oferta 2

workedExample.label: Compare
workedExample.work: 0.59 > 0.57, so Deal 2 is the better buy
workedExample.workEs: 0.59 > 0.57, así que la oferta 2 es la mejor compra

extending.correctWork: To find cost per pound, divide price by pounds: $8.75 ÷ 5 = $1.75 per lb, $5.10 ÷ 3 = $1.70 per lb. Deal 2 ($1.70/lb) is still the better buy — but the correct unit rates are dollars per pound, not pounds per dollar.
hints: The student divided quantity by price instead of price by quantity.
For 'cost per pound,' divide dollars by pounds: $8.75 ÷ 5 = $1.75/lb.
extending.titleEs: Encuentra el error de tasa unitaria
extending.explanation: The first unit-rate step divided pounds by dollars, which gives pounds per dollar instead of the cost per pound the question asks about. Dividing price by weight gives $8.75 ÷ 5 = $1.75 per pound and $5.10 ÷ 3 = $1.70 per pound, so Deal 2 is cheaper — the same choice, now backed by the rate that was actually requested.
extending.explanationEs: El primer paso de tasa unitaria dividió libras entre dólares, lo que da libras por dólar en vez del costo por libra que pide la pregunta. Dividir el precio entre el peso da $8.75 ÷ 5 = $1.75 por libra y $5.10 ÷ 3 = $1.70 por libra, así que la Oferta 2 es más barata: la misma elección, ahora respaldada por la tasa que en verdad se pedía.
extending.correctWorkEs: Para encontrar el costo por libra, divide el precio entre las libras: $8.75 ÷ 5 = $1.75 por lb, $5.10 ÷ 3 = $1.70 por lb. La oferta 2 ($1.70/lb) sigue siendo la mejor compra — pero las tasas unitarias correctas son dólares por libra, no libras por dólar.

extending.title: (Lesson 3.9) Find Marcus's Mistake
hints: Look at Step 3. What operation should you use with the multiplier?
To keep ratios equivalent, you multiply both parts by the same number — not add.
extending.explanation: In the "Apply to both parts" step Marcus adds the multiplier instead of multiplying by it. Since 5 became 20, the scale factor is × 4, so the first part must be 3 × 4 = 12, giving 12 cups : 20 cups. His 7:20 does not simplify to 3:5, which confirms the ratios are not equivalent.
extending.explanationEs: En el paso "Apply to both parts" Marcus suma el multiplicador en lugar de multiplicar por él. Como 5 pasó a 20, el factor de escala es × 4, así que la primera parte debe ser 3 × 4 = 12, lo que da 12 tazas : 20 tazas. Su 7:20 no se simplifica a 3:5, lo que confirma que las razones no son equivalentes.

extending.title: (Lesson 3.10) Find the Conversion Error
extending.correctWork: Since 3 feet = 1 yard, you divide by 3 (not multiply). 6 ÷ 3 = 2 yards.
hints: You're going from a smaller unit (feet) to a larger unit (yards). Should you multiply or divide?
Converting to a larger unit gives a smaller number. 6 feet ÷ 3 = 2 yards.
extending.explanation: Feet are smaller than yards, so 6 feet has to become a smaller number of yards, not a bigger one. Since 3 feet make 1 yard, divide: 6 ÷ 3 = 2 yards. Multiplying by 3 moved in the wrong direction and produced 18 yards, which is 9 times too long.
extending.explanationEs: Los pies son más pequeños que las yardas, así que 6 pies debe convertirse en un número menor de yardas, no mayor. Como 3 pies forman 1 yarda, se divide: 6 ÷ 3 = 2 yardas. Multiplicar por 3 fue en la dirección equivocada y dio 18 yardas, que es 9 veces demasiado largo.
extending.correctWorkEs: Como 3 pies = 1 yarda, se divide entre 3 (no se multiplica). 6 ÷ 3 = 2 yardas.
